business.title: Self-medication with GLP-1 receptor agonists among Brazilian Adults: findings from a web-based survey
business.description: Background: The popularity of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for weight loss has increased significantly in recent years, raising concerns about self-medication with these medications. Objective: To assess the proportion and identify factors associated with GLP-1 RA use without medical prescription among GLP-1 RA users in Brazil. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted through a self-administered online questionnaire including adults aged 18 years or older residing in Brazil who reported current or past use of GLP-1 RAs for weight loss. We reported the proportion of self-medication and explored associated factors using Poisson regression with robust variance, adjusting for potential confounders. Results: A total of 860 participants were included (mean age: 39.46 ± 10.61 years; 82.0% female; 47.1% with obesity). The proportion of self-medication with GLP-1 RA was 23.8% (95% CI: 21.1–26.8%). Predictors of self-medication included not having obesity (PR = 1.45; 95% CI: 1.13–1.89), not attending physical training centers (PR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.23–1.96), and working in healthcare-related professions (PR = 1.45; 95% CI: 1.14–1.84). Conversely, being married (PR = 0.73; 95% CI: 0.57–0.94), having diabetes (PR = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.18–0.70), or having eating disorders (PR = 0.72; 95% CI, 0.34–0.97) were associated with lower self-medication rates. Conclusion: Almost one in four users reported using GLP-1 RAs without medical prescription. This practice was more frequent among individuals without obesity, those not attending physical training centers, and healthcare professionals.

business.title: Experimental investigation on thermal characterization of PCM-modified hollow blocks for passive thermal regulation in buildings
business.description: The high energy consumption in buildings motivates the need for sustainable thermal management techniques, such as Phase Change Materials. By evaluating the possibility of using an organic Phase Change Material, beeswax with a melting range of 34–36 °C, in hollow concrete blocks for the passive control of indoor building temperatures through the absorption and release of energy in the form of heat of fusion. The beeswax is microencapsulated with a linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) shell via a coacervation method. The microencapsulated Phase Change Material (MEPCM) is then incorporated into the blocks utilizing a 1:5 cement-to-fine aggregate ratio and a water-to-cement (W/C) ratio of 0.45, replacing 1.5% of the cement by weight. Three additional block groups were designed using 1.5% lime and 1.5% ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) as alternatives for comparative analysis, which exhibit higher compressive strength than standard blocks. The compressive strength is 3.60 N/mm² for blocks containing the microencapsulated Phase Change Material, compared with 2.76 N/mm² for standard blocks. The blocks containing the microencapsulated Phase Change Material have the lowest water absorption and moisture movement. The blocks containing the microencapsulated Phase Change Material have the lowest thermal conductivity and the highest thermal resistivity compared to the standard blocks. X-ray Diffraction and Scanning Electron Microscopy tests confirmed the integrity of the microencapsulation and hydration processes. The blocks containing the microencapsulated Phase Change Material have been confirmed to be an effective means of storing renewable energy for building temperature control.

business.title: Exendin-4 improves neurodevelopmental outcome after neonatal germinal matrix hemorrhage
business.description: Germinal matrix hemorrhage (GMH) is a common complication in premature infants and is associated with a high risk of neurodevelopmental impairment and mortality. Currently, there are no specific neuroprotective treatments available. Exendin-4 is a drug used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, and it has shown neuroprotective effects in several neurological disorders including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease. In this study, we used the preterm postnatal day 5 rat model of GMH to evaluate whether exendin-4 exerts neuroprotective effects in this setting. Our results show that in the acute phase, exendin-4 reduced microglial activation, caspase-3 activation, p53 expression, AIF-associated cell death, MMP-9 expression, and neutrophil infiltration into the hemorrhage site. Exendin-4 treatment improved neurodevelopmental outcomes in both negative geotaxis and eye-opening latency when compared to saline-treated GMH controls, and conferred gray and white matter protection as early as 48 h after injury, with persistent neuroprotection observed at 5, 11, and 35 days after GMH. Exendin-4-treated animals also showed significant recovery of motor function in the rotarod test. In summary, this study demonstrates that exendin-4 reduces brain injury in a rat model of GMH in both the short and long term and is associated with improved neurological outcome.

science.description: Self-assembling, anthracene-based supramolecular nanofibers can enable excitons to migrate hundreds of nanometers, according to a new experimental finding by researchers at Science Tokyo. science.title: Trace element concentrations in two oribatid mite species and their associated soil and moss habitats
science.description: Oribatid mites (Acari: Oribatida) are soil-dwelling arthropods that contribute to decomposition processes and nutrient cycling. This study presents a preliminary analytical assessment of trace element concentrations in oribatid mites and their associated environmental matrices. Two species were examined together with their corresponding soil and moss substrates using Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). Due to limited sample availability, pooled samples were used and the results were evaluated in a descriptive manner. The findings indicate the presence of both trace metals and essential elements in mite and substrate samples, with variations observed between species and environmental matrices. Elemental profiles of mites generally reflected those of their surrounding substrates, suggesting environmental exposure as a contributing factor. Differences between sample groups are reported as observed trends rather than statistically validated relationships. The data provide sample-based evidence of element accumulation patterns in oribatid mites; however, the extent and mechanisms of uptake cannot be conclusively determined within the scope of this study. The results are therefore interpreted as indicative rather than definitive. This work provides baseline data for future studies employing expanded sampling and quantitative analyses, and contributes to the understanding of trace element distribution in soil-associated microarthropods.

science.title: Building-level wastewater surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in the general, student and hospital-associated populations
science.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns were investigated in three wastewater catchments in Perugia, Central Italy: an urban wastewater treatment plant influent, a university building, and a large hospital, used as proxies for the general, student, and hospital-associated populations, respectively. Monthly samples were collected from February to July 2025 and analysed using culture-based methods for third-generation cephalosporin resistant Escherichia coli (3GCR-Ec) and vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE), together with qPCR/dPCR quantification of selected antimicrobial resistance genes and intI1. 3GCR-Ec prevalence was comparable across the three populations, suggesting a broadly shared community-associated resistance background. In contrast, VRE showed a clear gradient, with the highest levels in hospital wastewater, intermediate values in urban wastewater, and the lowest levels in university wastewater. Molecular analyses identified a group of abundant markers consistently detected across populations (intI1, sul1, ermB and tetA) and a more variable group (qnrS, blaCTX-M, blaKPC and vanA) that better discriminated population-specific AMR profiles, particularly the hospital-associated one. These findings support the value of wastewater surveillance at different spatial resolutions for identifying AMR patterns associated with distinct population settings and expected antimicrobial pressures.
